input:
A square plate is contracting at the uniform rate 4 cm²/sec, then the rate at which the perimeter is decreasing, when side of the square is 20 cm, is

Options:
A. (1/5) cm/sec.
B. 4 cm/sec.
C. 2 cm/sec.
D. (2/5) cm/sec.

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Given that the area of a square is decreasing at 4 cm²/sec, find the rate of decrease of perimeter when the side length is 20 cm.
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Express perimeter in terms of area, then differentiate with respect to t. Or express dP/dt = (dP/dX)(dX/dt) and link dX/dt to dA/dt.

key_concepts: Area and perimeter of a square

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Write P = 4√A, differentiate with respect to t using chain rule, substitute dA/dt = -4 and X = 20.
logical_steps: Step 1: Express area A = X² and perimeter P = 4X
Step 3: Differentiate P with respect to t

step_1_define_quantities.A: X²  (area of square with side X)

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: dP/dt = (2/X)(dA/dt) = (2/20)(−4) = −2/5. The negative sign confirms perimeter is decreasing, and the magnitude is 2/5 cm/sec ✓
